images.title: Half covered the day before full
images.purpose: Compares the pond on day 29, half covered, with day 30, fully covered, because the lotuses double each day.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. Two large round ponds side by side with a curved arrow from the left pond to the right pond.
images.exact_structure: Two equal circles side by side, outlined in dark outline. Left circle: exactly its left half filled flat reddish purple (#CC79A7) (lotus cover), the right half plain white; the label 'day 29' above it, 'half' below it and '2²⁹' under that. Right circle: completely filled flat reddish purple (#CC79A7); the label 'day 30' above it, 'full' below it and '2³⁰' under that. One curved amber (#E69F00) arrow from the left circle to the right circle with the label '× 2' on it. Exactly 2 circles, 1 arrow. No individual flowers drawn.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: If it doubles every day, the day before full it was half full.
images.description: Compares the pond on day 29, half covered, with day 30, fully covered, because the lotuses double each day.
images.context: Starting from 1 lotus: 2 to the power 30 lotuses when full and 2 to the power 29 when half covered; doubling 2 to the power 29 gives 2 to the power 30.
images.teaching_notes: Day 15 is the common wrong guess; the picture shows only the last doubling.

image_decisions.why: The half to full doubling in one day is the whole insight of the pond puzzle.
